algorithm: A sequence of steps used to solve a problem.
api: An interface through which software components communicate.
argument: A value supplied when calling a function.
boolean: A value that is either true or false.
class: A definition of the data and behavior of objects.
compiler: A program that translates source code into another form.
database: An organized collection of stored data.
debugging: Finding and fixing errors in a program.
dictionary: A collection that maps unique keys to values.
django: A Python framework for building web applications.
exception: An event that interrupts normal program execution.
function: A reusable block of code that performs a task.
inheritance: Creating a class based on an existing class.
iteration: Repeating an operation over items or steps.
json: A text format for exchanging structured data.
list: An ordered, mutable collection of items.
loop: A construct that repeats a block of instructions.
module: A file containing reusable Python definitions.
object: An instance containing state and behavior.
python: A programming language with readable syntax.
recursion: Solving a problem by calling the same function on smaller cases.
tuple: An ordered, immutable collection of items.
variable: A name bound to a value in a program.
